Papers to read:

- **Collins, Koehler & Lynch (2024)** — *Methods That Support the Validation of Agent-Based Models*.
  Use this as your map of the modern ABM validation literature. It reviews multiple validation approaches and explicitly discusses the lack of one accepted procedure.

<!-- -->

- **Sargent — Verification and Validation of Simulation Models.**
  This gives you the broader simulation literature, rather than starting from ABMs.

- **Bayarri et al. (2007) — A Framework for Validation of Computer Models.**
  This is where I would start thinking statistically about comparison with physical/real observations.

- **Kennedy & O'Hagan (2001) — Bayesian Calibration of Computer Models.**\
  Focus on the distinction between
  wrong parametersandmodel discrepancy.\\text{wrong parameters}
  \\quad\\text{and}\\quad
  \\text{model discrepancy}.

<!-- -->

- **Windrum, Fagiolo & Moneta (2007)** — empirical validation of ABMs.
  This is useful because they explicitly discuss unresolved empirical-validation problems.

- **Belfrage et al. (2024)** — credibility of ABMs for policy use.\

  This pushes the question from “does it fit?” toward “can we trust conclusions drawn from it?”

For each paper,

Citation:

What problem is this paper solving?

What does "validation" mean here?

What data from reality are used?

How is the simulator compared with reality?

How are uncertainty and stochasticity handled?

How do they decide the model is adequate?
